newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian court to rule on child case magistrate.
newsitem.headline: Belgian court to rule on child case magistrate.

text.p: Belgium's highest court is expected to decide on Wednesday whether the magistrate leading the probe into the child sex abuse scandal has been legally compromised and must therefore pull out of the case.

Magistrate Jean-Marc Connerotte and public prosecutor Michel Bourlet are accused by lawyers for two of the 13 people charged of having shown bias by accepting a free meal from a group specialising in helping the parents of missing children.

National news agency Belga quoted judicial sources as saying that the Cour de Cassation's Prosecutor General, Eliane Liekendael, had already filed a report recommending that Connerotte be taken off the case. Belga added that this did not mean that the court would follow the recommendation.
Four girls have been found dead since mid-August on properties linked to Marc Dutroux, chief suspect in a scandal which has stunned Belgium.
The body of an accomplice whom Dutroux admits killing has also been found, and police are searching for at least seven other missing children.
The legal manoeuvre against Connerotte -- and by implication Bourlet -- has sparked a storm of public protest.

There have been marches in support of the pair through the streets of Neufchateau, the nerve centre of the investigations, and a petition against their removal from the case has already attracted 125,000 signatures.
Julien Pierre, the lawyer who was the first to lodge the formal complaint against Connerotte, has received death threats by telephone.
Pierre represents Dutroux who has been charged with murder, abduction and illegal imprisonment.

Whether or not the Cour de Cassation upholds the complaint against Connerotte, the early lodging of the motion for his removal opens the way for an appeal to the Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg. Such an appeal could add years to the case.
